title: Sun-Dried Tomato Pesto Panini Press
seoTitle: Sun-Dried Tomato Pesto Panini Press | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Pesto panini night—grilled chicken, pressed ciabatta, hall sandwich service
subtitle: Charred chicken breast, basil pesto, and pressed ciabatta for ten
description: Marinated chicken breasts grill to 165°F, slice, and stack on ciabatta with basil pesto, roasted red peppers, and provolone. Press on the griddle until crisp.

steps.title: Marinate chicken
steps.instruction: Pound breasts even. Marinate in olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and salt at least 1 hour. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use focaccia loaves, buffalo mozzarella, oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, grapeseed oil as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Use white balsamic vinegar, shallots as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Grill chicken
steps.instruction: Grill breasts at 425°F 6–7 minutes per side until 165°F internal. Rest 5 minutes and slice. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold sliced chicken
steps.instruction: Hold sliced chicken covered at 170°F in hotel pans until sandwich build. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Preheat the flat-top griddle
steps.instruction: Preheat griddle or flat-top to 375°F. Butter outer sides of ciabatta splits. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build panini
steps.instruction: Layer pesto, chicken slices, roasted pepper, provolone, and arugula on ciabatta. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Press on griddle
steps.instruction: Press sandwiches on griddle 3 minutes per side until bread is crisp and cheese melts. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold wrapped
steps.instruction: Hold finished panini wrapped in foil at 170°F up to 20 minutes. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Line for ten
steps.instruction: One panini per firefighter. Cut diagonal for service if desired. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Pound chicken even—thick spots dry while thin edges burn.
Butter outer bread, not the griddle, for even crisp.
Arugula after press if crew wants crunch; before press if they want wilted greens.
tonightSpread: Grilled chicken pesto panini with arugula.
Tomato soup shooters or simple chips.
leftovers: Slice panini into croutons for salad.
Chop chicken into pesto pasta next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Panini press on the griddle turns sandwich night into an event. Chicken holds sliced at 170°F; sandwiches build fast when crew sits down.
mealPrepNotes: Grill chicken at 425°F to 165°F, rest and slice. Hold sliced chicken at 170°F up to 30 minutes. Press panini to order or in batches at 375°F, 3 minutes each.
